Colour

Colours are named for their role, never their hue: --al-color-accent, not --al-teal. A role has one value per theme; components use roles only. Primitives (--al-color-cloud-98, --al-color-teal-51…) exist to build roles and are not used directly in components. Every primitive is used by a role (tests/system.test.js checks it).

Roles

The values below are the primitives each role points to, from tokens/tokens.json; a percentage is a translucent colour.

Token Use it for Light Dark
bg The page cloud 98 Night (slate 18)
surface Cards, panels, inputs, menus, dialogs white slate 21
surface-sunk Wells, hover, table head, affixes cloud 96 slate 24
text Body text, headings cloud 21 Pale (sand 93)
text-muted Hints, labels of secondary things, axes; stale figures cloud 45 sand 74
line Hairlines: dividers, card borders, table rules cloud 93 white 12%
line-strong Dividers that need to be seen (selected, dashed frames) cloud 21 at 40% white 40%
control The border of anything you operate: inputs, buttons, checkboxes slate 62 slate 62
accent Primary actions, links, focus, the selected tab; success teal 51 Mint (teal 83)
accent-hover A primary button, hovered teal 43 teal 91
on-accent Text on an accent or danger fill white slate 18
accent-wash Selected rows, highlighted totals teal 12% mint 12%
focus The focus outline teal 51 Mint
focus-on-inverse The focus outline on the inverse ground (bulk bar, toasts) Mint teal 51
danger, danger-wash Errors, and actions that destroy red 54 red 68
danger-hover A filled danger button, hovered red 46 red 78
warning, warning-wash Needs attention; unsaved amber 49 amber 80
success, success-wash Done, saved (the accent) teal 51 Mint
info, info-wash Neutral information blue 53 blue 80
inverse, on-inverse Toasts, tooltips, the bulk bar cloud 98 on cloud 21 slate 18 on Pale
backdrop Behind a modal dialog cloud 21 at 45% black 60%
chart-1…4 Chart series, in this order see below
chart-0 The neutral: tracks and grounds, never a series of data cloud 87 white 20%
tint-*-bg, tint-*-ink Tags, highlights, avatars: identity, never status see tint.md
pattern-line The tessellation's strands, in ink as on arabesquelabs.com cloud 21 at 26% white 20%
pattern-scaffold The tiling's polygons: the hero's scaffolding while it draws in, and the construction figure cloud 21 at 12% white 10%
pattern-focal The hero's focal tile the accent the accent
pattern-focal-fill Inside the focal tile's star teal at 16% mint at 16%

All tokens are prefixed: var(--al-color-surface).

Rules

  • Contrast is computed, not judged. scripts/build.mjs measures every pair the system relies on, in both themes, and the build fails if any falls short: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for control borders, focus (on every ground it can be drawn on, the inverse one too) and chart marks. Translucent grounds (washes) are measured on both the page and the surface, and the worse counts. The results are in ../contrast.md.
  • Hairlines aren't boundaries. line is decoration (1.3:1), so anything a person has to find — an input, a checkbox, a button — is drawn in control (3:1 or better against every ground).
  • Colour is never the only signal. Every status has an icon and a word ("Saved", "Couldn't save"); errors have an icon and text; chart series have a key, and their values are in a table or tooltip.
  • Success shares the accent. Teal is the brand's one colour; "done" and "go" are the same idea here. It's always paired with a check icon and a word, so it never reads as a mere link.
  • No shadows. Depth comes from the surface steps (bg → surface → surface-sunk) and from borders.
  • One accent per view. The primary button, the current tab and links share it; don't add a second brand colour for emphasis.
  • Washes are tints of their role (danger-wash under a danger notice), and only behind text in the same role or text.

Themes

Light is the default. Dark follows prefers-color-scheme: dark, and data-theme="light|dark" on <html> overrides the system both ways (js/theme.js remembers the choice as al-theme). Dark is designed, not inverted: the accent lightens to Mint, danger and warning lighten to keep their contrast, and hairlines become translucent white so they sit on any surface.

With prefers-contrast: more, secondary text becomes body text, hairlines become control borders and focus thickens to 3px (css/base.css). With forced-colors: active, components fall back to system colours and keep their borders and focus (each component's CSS has its own rule where needed).

Charts

The series colours come from hunt's palette, checked for colour-vision deficiency (adjacent pairs ≥ 8 ΔE in OKLab under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia) with the dataviz validator, in each theme against its surface:

Order Light Dark
1 green #007a5c #3ba888
2 orange #c26300 #ca7e31
3 blue #3d73b6 #5188cd
4 raspberry #b8336a #d75b8f
0 track (not data) cloud 87 white 20%

Assign them in this order and never cycle: a fifth series folds into "Other", which takes the next series colour, not chart-0. chart-0 is too light to be read as data (it's under 3:1), so it's only for tracks and grounds. In markup, a mark's series is data-series="1" to "4" (see chart.md). A series keeps its colour when others are filtered out. Status colours (danger, warning, success) are never chart series.
